name: The Eternal Imperium of Aeterna
summary: Following the miraculous survival of the Western Empire through the stabilization of the Rhine frontier in the 5th century, Rome evolved into a bureaucratic maritime hegemon. By successfully integrating the Germanic tribes into a meritocratic civil service, the Empire avoided the fragmentation that plagued traditional histories. Today, the Senate of Rome governs a continuous Mediterranean and Atlantic civilization that spans from the sands of Mesopotamia to the reaches of Hibernia.
tech_level: The Empire utilizes advanced steam-pressurized hydraulic engineering and complex clockwork logistics to power its massive urban centers. Scholars have refined early analytical engines to automate the Imperial census and navigate the vast naval trade routes.
gov_type: The state operates as a technocratic absolute monarchy led by the Caesar-Consul who is advised by a permanent, meritocratic Senate. Provincial governance is maintained through a sophisticated legal framework that ensures uniform tax collection and civil rights for all citizens regardless of ethnic origin.

events.title: The Decree of Ravenna
events.description: Emperor Romulus Augustulus successfully negotiated a permanent land-grant treaty with Odoacer, transforming the Germanic foederati into a hereditary Roman professional soldier class. This agreement integrated the barbarian military strength directly into the imperial tax and command structure.
events.impact: The collapse of the Western military apparatus was averted, preventing the onset of the Dark Ages. It established the precedent for integrating peripheral tribes into the administrative backbone of the state.

events.title: The Great Aqueduct Expansion
events.description: Imperial engineers perfected high-pressure concrete casting to bridge the deeper valleys of Gaul and Hispania, allowing for the rapid urbanization of the northern provinces. This engineering feat facilitated the movement of grain and personnel, cementing the loyalty of the frontiers.
events.impact: It ensured that the northern territories remained economically tethered to the Roman core for centuries. The project sparked an architectural renaissance that defined Roman aesthetics for the next millennium.

events.title: The Treaty of Theodosius
events.description: The Eastern and Western halves of the Empire formalized a unified currency standard based on the standardized gold solidus. This economic merger eliminated trade barriers across the entirety of the Mediterranean basin.
events.impact: The unified currency prevented the economic instability that historically led to the rise of localized feudalism. It created a singular, invincible market that dominated all global trade until the discovery of the Americas.

events.title: The Atlantic Expedition of Claudius IV
events.description: Roman naval architects utilized advanced astronomical charts to guide a fleet of trireme-galleons across the Atlantic Ocean. Upon reaching the shores of modern-day Brazil, the legions established the province of Nova Roma.
events.impact: The discovery brought unprecedented wealth in silver and rubber to the Roman treasury. This massive influx of resources fueled the subsequent industrial shift within the Roman urban heartlands.

events.title: The Grand Synod of Rome
events.description: The Senate ratified the inclusion of the Trans-Atlantic Provinces into full legislative representation, effectively transforming the Empire into a global federation. This shift signaled the end of traditional expansionism and the beginning of a focus on interplanetary exploration.
events.impact: It solidified the social cohesion of a global populace living under a unified Pax Romana. The Empire now redirects its vast industrial output toward the colonization of the inner solar system.
